caveats: Terms 3-10 for votes, attendance and committee roles; rapporteurs from term 5; plenary speech from term 6 (speaking time from term 8); questions from term 7; reply times from term 8.
Every MP can be found; there are no ranked top or bottom lists. Distributions show all MPs.
Committee speech is not included (committee transcripts were not fetched). Question and reply texts were not fetched.
The club line is the plurality of the club's YES, NO and ABSTAIN votes (NA on a tie); unaffiliated MPs have none. Rebellion is a vote that differs from a defined line.
Composite clubs hold more than one party (Party tracker); rebellion inside them often marks a party faction rather than individual dissent.
Term 3's vote types are unreliable; rebellion by vote type is reported for terms 4-10 only. Twelve term-3 ballots (failed the tally check) are left out of vote measures.

Attendance is the share of roll calls an MP voted in. Days with missed votes, excused and unexcused, come from the API's sitting-day statistics, which also count ON_LIST ballots, so the two sources count slightly differently. Term 9 includes remote voting from 2020.

The API's club tables hold only the clubs that existed at the end of each term, so club functions are missing for clubs that split or merged during a term; club membership over time comes from the roll calls.

Interpellation signatories: position 1 is counted as first-signed; whether it is the lead signatory is unchecked. Repeat interpellations are counted separately. answerDelayedDays is never used; delays are computed from the sending date and the first reply that is not a prolongation request, for questions with one recipient.
A reply is late if it arrives more than 21 days after sending; the 'extended' version adds 14 days for a question with a prolongation request on record (the length is an assumption).

Ministers, secretaries and under-secretaries of state who spoke as such (terms 6-10) and the Marshals of the Sejm (a hand-kept list, flagged for the whole term) are flagged and left out of distribution medians. Their attendance and speech are not comparable with ordinary MPs'.
Statement counts are not comparable between terms 6-7 and 8-10; word counts are. Words cover statements of at least 40 words.

Bills: the API names no MP sponsors, so bills give context (government against MPs' bills, topics, passage) and no per-MP measure. Term 10 is still running; its pending bills are not failures. The API's veto stage is incomplete for 2015-23, so there is no veto measure.
Ideal points (terms 5-10) are the polarisation project's linked dynamic IRT positions (standardised; negative towards PO/KO, positive towards PiS).
